messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Zh in mirt personfit
parts:
Hi Taeyoung,

I've cc'd your question to the mirt-package forum here.

Zh is theoretically distributed as a Gaussian, but unfortunately due to measurement error it generally isn't in practice. The PerFit package (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/PerFit/index.html) has some adjustments to fix this though, and I don't really plan to add them to mirt any time soon (person-fit stats are not my area of interest). HTH.

Phil

On Thu, Apr 13, 2017 at 5:35 AM, Taeyoung Kim <tki...@buffalo.edu> wrote:
Hi Phil,

I am a "mirt" user. That's an awesome package!

I have a quick question for you. How is Zh interpreted, something like higher Zh indicates better/poorer person fit? I saw the original paper you cited (i.e. Drasgow et al) but not sure.

Thank you in advance,
Taeyoung

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Re: Zh in mirt personfit
parts:
Hi Taeyoung,

Higher Zh indicates meant too overly fitted. But some works of studies focused on the detect aberrant response with lower Zh values. My opinion is lower Zh values means some cases unreliable responded if your model has not the improper solution; higher Zh is ignorable in practices. Drasgow and colleges (1985) focused on lower Zh sides.

Seongho
